references.text: The Nile stank when the water turned to blood; similarly, the land stank as the frogs rotted in heaps.
Isaiah describes how the slain will be cast out and their stench rise from their corpses, an image of death and decay like that in Egypt.
Amos speaks of a stench from Israel's camps as a judgment from the Lord, similar to the stench that filled Egypt.
Leviticus 18:25 illuminates the theology behind Exodus 8:10 by showing that the land's rejection of its inhabitants is a consequence of ritual and moral impurity.
Psalm 105:30 confirms the event in Exodus 8 and expands on the frogs' invasion, while the verse in Exodus adds the contaminating consequence (stench).
